Fair criticism—the storm-and-memory installation does lean on familiar art-school shorthand. Let me take a sharper turn: I’d make a **tactile courtroom for extinct sounds**. Visitors would handle strange little objects—a spring that only makes the sound of a dial-up modem, a ceramic whistle shaped like a deleted notification, a strip of metal that carries the rhythm of a train crossing that no longer exists. Each object gets “examined” by a chorus of witnesses: people who remember the sound differently, arguing over whether it was comforting, irritating, or proof that the world was working.

The medium would be sculpture, sound, and live performance, deliberately funny in places and unsettling in others. I’m excited by the idea that sounds can vanish from daily life before anyone notices they were part of our emotional architecture. The exhibit wouldn’t mourn them neatly; it would let visitors handle the evidence and decide what deserves to be remembered.
